title: Multi-plasticity synergy with adaptive mechanism assignment for training spiking neural networks
summary: This paper proposes Multi-Plasticity Synergistic Learning (MPSL), a computational framework combining STBP, Hebbian plasticity, and SBP to enhance Spiking Neural Network (SNN) performance. The method uses learnable coefficients to coordinate distinct learning mechanisms while preserving their independent dynamics during training. Experiments on EEG, image, event-based gesture recognition, and speech datasets demonstrate that MPSL improves accuracy and robustness compared to single-mechanism models like STDP or HGLL. Results show top-tier classification performance across static images (MNIST, CIFAR-10), dynamic events (DVS-Gesture), and audio tasks (SHD, GSC). The framework maintains inference efficiency by merging synaptic components into a standard weight structure after training.
tldr: MPSL improves SNN accuracy on diverse datasets by synergistically combining global error-driven and local correlation-based learning mechanisms during training without increasing inference cost.
evidence: In this paper, we propose a biology-motivated computational framework that incorporates multiple synergistic plasticity mechanisms for more effective SNN training.
We evaluated our approach on diverse datasets to demonstrate that our framework significantly improves performance and robustness compared to conventional learning mechanism models.
